slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that build quietly
unshakeable confidence

saying i don't know

next time, say i don't know out loud instead of nodding along. people trust you more when they see you're comfortable admitting what you haven't learned yet.

apologising once

when you're wrong, apologise once, briefly and without long excuses. a short, honest sorry shows strength, while a long, nervous one only sounds like begging.

learning what you pretend to know

spend 5 minutes a day on something you always pretend to understand, like the stock market or black holes. understanding things for real makes you so much more confident.
slides.texte_sophia:
learning what you pretend to know

i used to nod along to things i didn't understand. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, black holes or the stock market, and i stopped pretending.

slides.texte_overlay:
asking directly

for one week, ask for exactly what you want instead of hinting: the window seat, more time, a day off. hints get ignored, but clear requests get answered.

laughing at yourself

when you trip, spill something or say something silly, laugh first. someone who can laugh at their own mistakes looks completely at ease in their skin.
